Vallabha
(A. D. 1473-1531)
------------------------------------------
Vallabha or Vallabhācārya was one of the more prominent teachers of Vaiṣṇa-vism who contributed considerably to the cult of Kṛṣṇabhakti or devotion to Kṛṣna.
VallabhācāryaHe was born at Campāraṇya (near the modern Raipur in the Chattisgarh State) to the couple Lakṣmaṇabhaṭṭa and Yellamma who were originally from the Telugu country (Andhra Pradesh).
Since Lakṣmaṇabhaṭṭa had settled down at काशी (the modern Banaras), वल्लभ got the opportunity for very good एदुचतिओन्. Trained by विष्णुचित्त, he proved to be a child prodigy by mastering the वेदस्, the वेदाङ्गस् and the six systems of philosophy as also other scriptures like the Bhagavadgītā, and the Bhāgavata.
He lost his ड़थेर् at the age of eleven. This led to the break-up of the home at Banaras. From this time—even though he was quite young—he undertook a पिल्ग्रिमगे of the whole of India three times, lasting for about twenty years. During his sojourn to South India, he came to Vijayanagar when the famous king कृष्ण-devarāya (A. D. 1488-1529) had just taken over as the king.
Though a boy of twelve years वल्लभ soon established his mastery over the scriptures and philosophies by defeating many a scholar in debates. He was honoured by the king with the rite of kanakābhiṣeka (showering with gold coins).
Other places he visited included some of the well-known places of पिल्ग्रिमगे. They were: Śrīśaila, तिरुपति, काञ्चीपुरम्, मदुरै, रामेश्वरम्, उडुपि, गोकर्ण (all in South India); Paṇḍharāpur, नासिक् and Tryambakeśvar (in Maharashtra); द्वारका (in Gujarat); मथुरा and वृन्दाबन् (in western Uttar Pradesh); Himālayan centres such as Badarī, Kedār and Gaṅgotri; Gaṅgāsāgar and पुरी in eastern India.
After the second पिल्ग्रिमगे he married महालक्ष्मी, daughter of a pious ब्राह्मण Devadatta.
During one of his pilgrimages, वल्लभ had a wonderful divine experience. He received the command as to his mission of life from a divine sage who was a disciple of शाण्डिल्य, the great teacher of भक्ति.
He now started his own सम्प्रदाय or spiritual tradition—a new faith or a sect—at गोकुल (in the मथुरा-वृन्दाबन् region). He received an image of Govardhananātha (Boy कृष्ण in the act of lifting the गोवर्धन hill)—which emerged mysteriously out of a cave—from a saint Mādhavendra-पुरी, built a small temple for it and started its worship. Later on, a much bigger temple was built. Due to the Muslim invasions, the image was later—after वल्लभ’s time—shifted to Nāthdvāra near Udaipur (in Rajasthan). The temple there is now quite famous and the image is called Śrīnāthjī.
Vallabha considered कृष्ण as the highest God. He advocated his worship, especially as Bālakṛṣṇa (Boy-कृष्ण). Redemption can come only through his grace. The मन्त्र he gave to one and all was Śrikṛṣṇaḥ śaraṇaṁ mama.
His philosophy is known as शुद्धाद्वैत and the religious path as Puṣṭimārga (See BRAHMASŪTRAS and PUṢṬIMĀRGA).
Vallabha wrote several philosophical and devotional works. Among them the Aṇubhāṣya on the Brahmasūtras and Subodhinī on the Bhāgavata are famous. Unfortunately both are incomplete.
He took सṁन्यास during his last days from Mādhavendrapurī and gave up his body in the गङ्गा at Hanumānghāṭ in वाराणसी (Banaras).
His second son Viṭṭhalanātha became the leader of the sect after वल्लभ.

Vālakhilyas
------------------------------------------
The वालखिल्यस् were great sages (60,000 in number) born of the parents Kratu and Kriyādevī. They were of the size of a thumb! Once they helped the sage कश्यप in the performance of a sacrifice and became tired. इन्द्र who saw them in that condition laughed at them incurring their wrath. They cursed him that Garuḍa—born out of their तपस् (austerity)—would punish him for his arrogance.

Vālmīki
------------------------------------------
Vālmīki is the sage who has immortalised himself and his work, the Rāmāyaṇa.
According to one version, he was a प्रजापति, a son of Pracetas.
According to another version (Adhyatma Rāmāyaṇa, Ayodhyākāṇḍa 6.57-78) he was a ब्राह्मण by birth, but was brought up by robbers. Once, the सप्तर्षिस् (the Seven Sages) came to his forest and were accosted by him. Contact with these holy sages converted him to pursue a life of devotion to राम. Since he sat in meditation for many years, an anthill grew over him. When the sages—on their return journey—found him in that condition they poured water over the anthill, released him and blessed him with a new name ‘Vālmīki’ (one who emerged out of an anthill).
Vālmīki established his own आश्रम and started living there. One day when he came to the river Tamasā for bath, he saw a hunter kill a male bird and heard the piteous wailings of the female. Immediately he cursed the hunter, which curse emerged from his mouth in the form of a śloka (a verse in the anuṣṭubh metre). Wondering at this phenomenon he returned to his hut. Then ब्रह्मा, the creator appeared before him and commanded him to compose the detailed life-story of राम for which the basic material was given by the sage नारद. Thus came into existence the great epic Rāmāyaṇa.
When राम banished सीता due to public criticism, लक्ष्मण left her near the hermitage of वाल्मीकि. She was pregnant at that time. She delivered twins who were christened by वाल्मीकि as लव and कुश. It was Vālmīkī who brought them up, educated them and also taught them the Rāmāyaṇa with मुसिच्. Later he took सीता and the children to राम and offered them back to him. While सीता entered the womb of मोथेर् Earth, the sons were accepted by राम.
